title: Dialogue mapping the help-seeking behaviours of university students who have experienced gender-based violence
abstract: University students are among the age group with the highest incidence and prevalence of gender-based violence (GBV). The consequences of GBV are extreme and multilayered; however, a mediating effect on the negative consequences associated with experiencing GBV includes seeking help from formal and informal resources. To date, little is known regarding the reasons for university students accessing certain resources and services. This study explored Canadian undergraduate students’ help-seeking behaviours following experiences of GBV. Seventeen semi-structured interviews took place in the spring of 2023. Interviews were analysed using summative content analysis and dialogue mapping, with students identifying potential GBV resources including (1) at the host institution, (2) in the community and (3) from informal resources. Barriers and facilitators for university students when accessing resources following experiences of GBV are discussed. These findings offer a roadmap for institutions seeking to create more inclusive, effective and survivor-centred responses to GBV.
